insights.topic: Deterministic purchase signals vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The protocol has produced 11,033 cryptographically verified purchase receipts — each one a confirmed transaction, not an inferred intent. At $5+ CPM, the ad industry pays a premium for probabilistic signals that cannot match the certainty of a verified receipt.
Seven-day GMV crossed $100K for the first time on April 7 and reached $199,939 by April 13 — a near-doubling in six days. That pace, if sustained, puts $1M cumulative GMV before April 16.

insights.topic: Category breadth expanding beyond physical retail
insights.insight: As of April 9, the network recorded its first SaaS subscription receipt, extending verified purchase signals beyond grocery, dining, fuel, and general retail. Brand marketers targeting digital-product buyers now have a confirmed signal category that did not exist in this dataset two weeks ago.

The April 12 heartbeat logged 22 active CBSAs in a single window — a network record — with Wisconsin, North Carolina, and Rhode Island non-metro areas entering simultaneously. Brands with rural or regional footprints have a growing addressable signal base here.

insights.topic: Top brand representation signals retail breadth
insights.insight: The 14-day brand list spans mass retail (Walmart, 174 receipts), warehouse/bulk (Costco, 56), pharmacy (CVS, 54), and auto parts (NAPA, 66) — a cross-category mix that reflects everyday household spend, not niche or luxury purchasing behavior.

insights.topic: High-AOV purchase events within the verified set
insights.insight: The April 9 burst added $56,064 in GMV from only 42 receipts — an average of roughly $1,335 per receipt in that window. That average transaction size is a signal quality indicator: the verified set includes high-value purchases that probabilistic targeting cannot confirm occurred.
